messages:
ana: Heads up — long-context runs on the private A100 cluster are showing steady GPU memory growth tied to KV slot allocations. Not an OOM yet but after ~40k tokens memory climbs ~1.2GB/hour.

mike: Interesting. I saw a similar slow drift in dedicated last week but it stabilized after we bumped the batching window. Could be reuse heat vs churn.

rami: Can you paste the profile? small snippets help. Is the growth in host page faults or GPU-side allocation?

ana: attaching quick summary: kernel traces show repeated mmap()/munmap() pairs and a slow increase in anonymous RSS over time. KV slot reuse ratio downshifted from ~0.92 to ~0.6 on long sessions.

li: vpc note — private runs are behind a firewall + MTU 1500. Onprem infra team mentioned jumbo frames are disabled for those racks; could increase fragmentation. Smaller MTU -> more allocations observed in past kernel experiments.

mike: that matches a hypothesis: fragmentation prevents hugepage coalescing so the kernel falls back to many small allocations, which interferes with our slab/allocator heuristics. When our runtime chooses kernel variant A (fast GEMM path) we keep a larger working set and reuse; variant B (compat fallback) triggers more transient KV frames.

rami: can we correlate with kernel selection logs? The runtime emits kernel_profile events in /var/log/redwood/runtime.log. If fallback rate spikes, that would explain a different allocation pattern.

ana: I grepped the logs: during long contexts we have ~0.3% fallback initially, but after 30k tokens fallback rises to ~7% and stays elevated.

li: elevated fallback + MTU=1500 seems like a bad combo. Suggests page-sway: more small page churn -> slab whispering -> slower backfills.

mike: also check batching heuristics. We had a canary where batching window was reduced from 45ms -> 15ms to improve p95. That reduced request coalescing and increased unique KV frames touched per second. So lower latency config can increase churn.

sophie: so two knobs: batching window and kernel selection fallback. Actionable items: 1) reproduce on a hosted-like env but force MTU=1500, 2) run with forced kernel variant to see if growth disappears, 3) heap/profile to catch which allocator buckets grow.

ana: repro plan for tomorrow: run longctx driver with --tokens 100k, enable runtime trace, toggle batching to 15/45/100ms, toggle kernel_force=avx2/compat. Collect /proc/vmstat, slabtop, nvidia-smi dmon.

rami: quick command for capture: 
```
perf record -a -g -o /tmp/perf.data -- sleep 600
sudo slabtop -o -s c -n 50 > /tmp/slab.out
watch -n1 'cat /proc/vmstat | grep -E "pgfree|pgfault|pgmajfault"' > /tmp/vmstat.log &
```

mike: also capture runtime's KV metrics: kv_reuse_ratio, kv_allocs_per_min, kv_evictions_total, kv_page_faults. Those map well to the slab counters.

li: FYI infra will try enabling jumbo frames on a test rack tomorrow AM so we can validate the MTU hypothesis. If that helps, we can document a VPC note for Private installs.

sophie: if kernel fallback is the root cause we should tweak our kernel selector to prefer the stable path under longctx workloads or fall back earlier to pre-warm the right buffers.

ana: noted. For tracking: I'll open a perf issue with metrics attached and tag infra + runtime. Expected ETA: repro by EOD tomorrow, initial mitigation (tweak batching) within 48h.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy of runtime v2.14.3 completed to private-canary-3 at 1751010000. No errors.

mike: perfect. If canary sees the same slope we need to instrument more. If not, maybe a config drift in that rack.

rami: one more thought — on onprem drivers we've seen delayed cudaMalloc garbage collection when the driver patch level mismatches CUDA runtime. Could be delayed GPU-side free causing host-side allocations to pile up. Please include driver+cuda versions in the capture.

ana: will include driver/cuda, kernel version, runtime logs, slabtop and the small perf trace. Thanks — I'll post results in this thread after the runs.

sophie: thanks all. Quick checklist: reproduce, capture kernel+slab+kv metrics, test MTU jumbo, test forced kernel variant, test batching windows.

li: tagging infra: @infra please coordinate jumbo frames on test rack 7 and provide NIC ethtool settings.

ana: @infra thanks — ping me when ready and I'll kick off the run.
